sphinx/addnodes.py:457:
sphinx/addnodes.py:458:class pending_xref_condition(nodes.Inline, nodes.TextElement):
sphinx/addnodes.py:459:    """Node for cross-references that are used to choose appropriate
sphinx/addnodes.py:460:    content of the reference by conditions on the resolving phase.
sphinx/addnodes.py:461:
sphinx/addnodes.py:462:    When the :py:class:`pending_xref` node contains one or more
sphinx/addnodes.py:463:    **pending_xref_condition** nodes, the cross-reference resolver
sphinx/addnodes.py:464:    should choose the content of the reference using defined conditions
sphinx/addnodes.py:465:    in ``condition`` attribute of each pending_xref_condition nodes::
sphinx/addnodes.py:466:
sphinx/addnodes.py:467:        <pending_xref refdomain="py" reftarget="io.StringIO ...>
sphinx/addnodes.py:468:            <pending_xref_condition condition="resolved">
sphinx/addnodes.py:469:                <literal>
sphinx/addnodes.py:470:                    StringIO
sphinx/addnodes.py:471:            <pending_xref_condition condition="*">
sphinx/addnodes.py:472:                <literal>
sphinx/addnodes.py:473:                    io.StringIO
sphinx/addnodes.py:474:
sphinx/addnodes.py:475:    After the processing of cross-reference resolver, one of the content node
sphinx/addnodes.py:476:    under pending_xref_condition node is chosen by its condition and to be
sphinx/addnodes.py:477:    removed all of pending_xref_condition nodes::
sphinx/addnodes.py:478:
sphinx/addnodes.py:479:        # When resolved the cross-reference successfully
sphinx/addnodes.py:480:        <reference>
sphinx/addnodes.py:481:            <literal>
sphinx/addnodes.py:482:                StringIO
sphinx/addnodes.py:483:
sphinx/addnodes.py:484:        # When resolution is failed
sphinx/addnodes.py:485:        <reference>
sphinx/addnodes.py:486:            <literal>
sphinx/addnodes.py:487:                io.StringIO
sphinx/addnodes.py:488:
sphinx/addnodes.py:489:    .. note:: This node is only allowed to be placed under pending_xref node.
sphinx/addnodes.py:490:              It is not allows to place it under other nodes.  In addition,
sphinx/addnodes.py:491:              pending_xref node must contain only pending_xref_condition
sphinx/addnodes.py:492:              nodes if it contains one or more pending_xref_condition nodes.
sphinx/addnodes.py:493:
sphinx/addnodes.py:494:    The pending_xref_condition node should have **condition** attribute.
sphinx/addnodes.py:495:    Domains can be store their individual conditions into the attribute to
sphinx/addnodes.py:496:    filter contents on resolving phase.  As a reserved condition name,
sphinx/addnodes.py:497:    ``condition="*"`` is used for the fallback of resolution failure.
sphinx/addnodes.py:498:    Additionally, as a recommended condition name, ``condition="resolved"``
sphinx/addnodes.py:499:    is used for the representation of resolstion success in the intersphinx
sphinx/addnodes.py:500:    module.
sphinx/addnodes.py:501:
sphinx/addnodes.py:502:    .. versionadded:: 4.0
sphinx/addnodes.py:503:    """
sphinx/addnodes.py:504:

sphinx/application.py:796:                        objname: str = '', doc_field_types: List = [], override: bool = False
sphinx/application.py:797:                        ) -> None:
sphinx/application.py:798:        """Register a new object type.
sphinx/application.py:799:
sphinx/application.py:800:        This method is a very convenient way to add a new :term:`object` type
sphinx/application.py:801:        that can be cross-referenced.  It will do this:
sphinx/application.py:802:
sphinx/application.py:803:        - Create a new directive (called *directivename*) for documenting an
sphinx/application.py:804:          object.  It will automatically add index entries if *indextemplate*
sphinx/application.py:805:          is nonempty; if given, it must contain exactly one instance of
sphinx/application.py:806:          ``%s``.  See the example below for how the template will be
sphinx/application.py:807:          interpreted.
sphinx/application.py:808:        - Create a new role (called *rolename*) to cross-reference to these
sphinx/application.py:809:          object descriptions.
sphinx/application.py:810:        - If you provide *parse_node*, it must be a function that takes a
sphinx/application.py:811:          string and a docutils node, and it must populate the node with
sphinx/application.py:812:          children parsed from the string.  It must then return the name of the
sphinx/application.py:813:          item to be used in cross-referencing and index entries.  See the
sphinx/application.py:814:          :file:`conf.py` file in the source for this documentation for an
sphinx/application.py:815:          example.
sphinx/application.py:816:        - The *objname* (if not given, will default to *directivename*) names
sphinx/application.py:817:          the type of object.  It is used when listing objects, e.g. in search
sphinx/application.py:818:          results.
sphinx/application.py:819:
sphinx/application.py:820:        For example, if you have this call in a custom Sphinx extension::
sphinx/application.py:821:
sphinx/application.py:822:           app.add_object_type('directive', 'dir', 'pair: %s; directive')
sphinx/application.py:823:
sphinx/application.py:824:        you can use this markup in your documents::
sphinx/application.py:825:
sphinx/application.py:826:           .. rst:directive:: function
sphinx/application.py:827:
sphinx/application.py:828:              Document a function.
sphinx/application.py:829:
sphinx/application.py:830:           <...>
sphinx/application.py:831:
sphinx/application.py:832:           See also the :rst:dir:`function` directive.
sphinx/application.py:833:
sphinx/application.py:834:        For the directive, an index entry will be generated as if you had prepended ::
sphinx/application.py:835:
sphinx/application.py:836:           .. index:: pair: function; directive
sphinx/application.py:837:
sphinx/application.py:838:        The reference node will be of class ``literal`` (so it will be rendered
sphinx/application.py:839:        in a proportional font, as appropriate for code) unless you give the
sphinx/application.py:840:        *ref_nodeclass* argument, which must be a docutils node class.  Most
sphinx/application.py:841:        useful are ``docutils.nodes.emphasis`` or ``docutils.nodes.strong`` --
sphinx/application.py:842:        you can also use ``docutils.nodes.generated`` if you want no further
sphinx/application.py:843:        text decoration.  If the text should be treated as literal (e.g. no
sphinx/application.py:844:        smart quote replacement), but not have typewriter styling, use
sphinx/application.py:845:        ``sphinx.addnodes.literal_emphasis`` or
sphinx/application.py:846:        ``sphinx.addnodes.literal_strong``.
sphinx/application.py:847:
sphinx/application.py:848:        For the role content, you have the same syntactical possibilities as
sphinx/application.py:849:        for standard Sphinx roles (see :ref:`xref-syntax`).
sphinx/application.py:850:
sphinx/application.py:851:        If *override* is True, the given object_type is forcedly installed even if
sphinx/application.py:852:        an object_type having the same name is already installed.
sphinx/application.py:853:
sphinx/application.py:854:        .. versionchanged:: 1.8
sphinx/application.py:855:           Add *override* keyword.
sphinx/application.py:856:        """
sphinx/application.py:857:        self.registry.add_object_type(directivename, rolename, indextemplate, parse_node,
sphinx/application.py:858:                                      ref_nodeclass, objname, doc_field_types,

sphinx/builders/epub3.py:124:        for node in navnodes:

sphinx/builders/linkcheck.py:582:    def limit_rate(self, response: Response) -> Optional[float]:
sphinx/builders/linkcheck.py:583:        next_check = None
sphinx/builders/linkcheck.py:584:        retry_after = response.headers.get("Retry-After")
sphinx/builders/linkcheck.py:585:        if retry_after:
sphinx/builders/linkcheck.py:586:            try:
sphinx/builders/linkcheck.py:587:                # Integer: time to wait before next attempt.
sphinx/builders/linkcheck.py:588:                delay = float(retry_after)
sphinx/builders/linkcheck.py:589:            except ValueError:
sphinx/builders/linkcheck.py:590:                try:
sphinx/builders/linkcheck.py:591:                    # An HTTP-date: time of next attempt.
sphinx/builders/linkcheck.py:592:                    until = parsedate_to_datetime(retry_after)
sphinx/builders/linkcheck.py:593:                except (TypeError, ValueError):
sphinx/builders/linkcheck.py:594:                    # TypeError: Invalid date format.
sphinx/builders/linkcheck.py:595:                    # ValueError: Invalid date, e.g. Oct 52th.
sphinx/builders/linkcheck.py:596:                    pass
sphinx/builders/linkcheck.py:597:                else:
sphinx/builders/linkcheck.py:598:                    next_check = datetime.timestamp(until)
sphinx/builders/linkcheck.py:599:                    delay = (until - datetime.now(timezone.utc)).total_seconds()
sphinx/builders/linkcheck.py:600:            else:

sphinx/builders/linkcheck.py:603:        if next_check is None:
sphinx/builders/linkcheck.py:604:            max_delay = self.config.linkcheck_rate_limit_timeout
sphinx/builders/linkcheck.py:605:            try:
sphinx/builders/linkcheck.py:606:                rate_limit = self.rate_limits[netloc]
sphinx/builders/linkcheck.py:607:            except KeyError:
sphinx/builders/linkcheck.py:608:                delay = DEFAULT_DELAY
sphinx/builders/linkcheck.py:609:            else:
sphinx/builders/linkcheck.py:610:                last_wait_time = rate_limit.delay
sphinx/builders/linkcheck.py:611:                delay = 2.0 * last_wait_time
sphinx/builders/linkcheck.py:612:                if delay > max_delay and last_wait_time < max_delay:
sphinx/builders/linkcheck.py:613:                    delay = max_delay

sphinx/builders/linkcheck.py:615:                return None
sphinx/builders/linkcheck.py:616:            next_check = time.time() + delay

sphinx/config.py:171:    def convert_overrides(self, name: str, value: Any) -> Any:

sphinx/config.py:174:        else:
sphinx/config.py:175:            defvalue = self.values[name][0]
sphinx/config.py:176:            if self.values[name][2] == Any:
sphinx/config.py:177:                return value
sphinx/config.py:178:            elif self.values[name][2] == {bool, str}:
sphinx/config.py:179:                if value == '0':
sphinx/config.py:180:                    # given falsy string from command line option
sphinx/config.py:181:                    return False
sphinx/config.py:182:                elif value == '1':
sphinx/config.py:183:                    return True
sphinx/config.py:184:                else:
sphinx/config.py:185:                    return value
sphinx/config.py:186:            elif type(defvalue) is bool or self.values[name][2] == [bool]:
sphinx/config.py:187:                if value == '0':
sphinx/config.py:188:                    # given falsy string from command line option
sphinx/config.py:189:                    return False
sphinx/config.py:190:                else:
sphinx/config.py:191:                    return bool(value)
sphinx/config.py:192:            elif isinstance(defvalue, dict):
sphinx/config.py:193:                raise ValueError(__('cannot override dictionary config setting %r, '
sphinx/config.py:194:                                    'ignoring (use %r to set individual elements)') %
sphinx/config.py:195:                                 (name, name + '.key=value'))
sphinx/config.py:196:            elif isinstance(defvalue, list):

sphinx/config.py:198:            elif isinstance(defvalue, int):

sphinx/config.py:205:                return value
sphinx/config.py:206:            elif defvalue is not None and not isinstance(defvalue, str):

sphinx/config.py:403:def check_confval_types(app: "Sphinx", config: Config) -> None:
sphinx/config.py:404:    """check all values for deviation from the default value's type, since
sphinx/config.py:405:    that can result in TypeErrors all over the place NB.
sphinx/config.py:406:    """
sphinx/config.py:407:    for confval in config:
sphinx/config.py:408:        default, rebuild, annotations = config.values[confval.name]
sphinx/config.py:409:
sphinx/config.py:410:        if hasattr(default, '__call__'):
sphinx/config.py:411:            default = default(config)  # evaluate default value
sphinx/config.py:412:        if default is None and not annotations:
sphinx/config.py:413:            continue  # neither inferrable nor expliclitly annotated types
sphinx/config.py:414:
sphinx/config.py:415:        if annotations is Any:
sphinx/config.py:416:            # any type of value is accepted
sphinx/config.py:417:            pass
sphinx/config.py:418:        elif isinstance(annotations, ENUM):
sphinx/config.py:419:            if not annotations.match(confval.value):
sphinx/config.py:420:                msg = __("The config value `{name}` has to be a one of {candidates}, "
sphinx/config.py:421:                         "but `{current}` is given.")
sphinx/config.py:422:                logger.warning(msg.format(name=confval.name,
sphinx/config.py:423:                                          current=confval.value,
sphinx/config.py:424:                                          candidates=annotations.candidates))
sphinx/config.py:425:        else:
sphinx/config.py:426:            if type(confval.value) is type(default):
sphinx/config.py:427:                continue
sphinx/config.py:428:            if type(confval.value) in annotations:
sphinx/config.py:429:                continue
sphinx/config.py:430:
sphinx/config.py:431:            common_bases = (set(type(confval.value).__bases__ + (type(confval.value),)) &
sphinx/config.py:432:                            set(type(default).__bases__))
sphinx/config.py:433:            common_bases.discard(object)
sphinx/config.py:434:            if common_bases:
sphinx/config.py:435:                continue  # at least we share a non-trivial base class
sphinx/config.py:436:
sphinx/config.py:437:            if annotations:
sphinx/config.py:438:                msg = __("The config value `{name}' has type `{current.__name__}'; "
sphinx/config.py:439:                         "expected {permitted}.")
sphinx/config.py:440:                wrapped_annotations = ["`{}'".format(c.__name__) for c in annotations]
sphinx/config.py:441:                if len(wrapped_annotations) > 2:
sphinx/config.py:442:                    permitted = "{}, or {}".format(
sphinx/config.py:443:                        ", ".join(wrapped_annotations[:-1]),
sphinx/config.py:444:                        wrapped_annotations[-1])
sphinx/config.py:445:                else:
sphinx/config.py:446:                    permitted = " or ".join(wrapped_annotations)
sphinx/config.py:447:                logger.warning(msg.format(name=confval.name,
sphinx/config.py:448:                                          current=type(confval.value),
sphinx/config.py:449:                                          permitted=permitted))
sphinx/config.py:450:            else:
sphinx/config.py:451:                msg = __("The config value `{name}' has type `{current.__name__}', "
sphinx/config.py:452:                         "defaults to `{default.__name__}'.")
sphinx/config.py:453:                logger.warning(msg.format(name=confval.name,

sphinx/domains/cpp.py:61:
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:62:
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:63:    Signature Nodes and Tagnames
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:64:    ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:65:
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:66:    Each signature is in a desc_signature node, where all children are
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:67:    desc_signature_line nodes. Each of these lines will have the attribute
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:68:    'sphinx_line_type' set to one of the following (prioritized):
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:69:    - 'declarator', if the line contains the name of the declared object.
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:70:    - 'templateParams', if the line starts a template parameter list,
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:71:    - 'templateParams', if the line has template parameters
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:72:      Note: such lines might get a new tag in the future.
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:73:    - 'templateIntroduction, if the line is on the form 'conceptName{...}'
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:74:    No other desc_signature nodes should exist (so far).
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:75:
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:76:
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:77:    Grammar
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:78:    ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:79:
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:80:    See https://www.nongnu.org/hcb/ for the grammar,
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:81:    and https://github.com/cplusplus/draft/blob/master/source/grammar.tex,
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:82:    and https://github.com/cplusplus/concepts-ts
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:83:    for the newest grammar.
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:84:
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:85:    common grammar things:
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:86:        template-declaration ->
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:87:            "template" "<" template-parameter-list ">" declaration
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:88:        template-parameter-list ->
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:89:              template-parameter
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:90:            | template-parameter-list "," template-parameter
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:91:        template-parameter ->
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:92:              type-parameter
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:93:            | parameter-declaration # i.e., same as a function argument
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:94:
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:95:        type-parameter ->
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:96:              "class"    "..."[opt] identifier[opt]
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:97:            | "class"               identifier[opt] "=" type-id
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:98:            | "typename" "..."[opt] identifier[opt]
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:99:            | "typename"            identifier[opt] "=" type-id
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:100:            | "template" "<" template-parameter-list ">"
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:101:                "class"  "..."[opt] identifier[opt]
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:102:            | "template" "<" template-parameter-list ">"
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:103:                "class"             identifier[opt] "=" id-expression
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:104:            # also, from C++17 we can have "typename" in template templates
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:105:        templateDeclPrefix ->
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:106:            "template" "<" template-parameter-list ">"
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:107:
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:108:        simple-declaration ->
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:109:            attribute-specifier-seq[opt] decl-specifier-seq[opt]
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:110:                init-declarator-list[opt] ;
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:111:        # Make the semicolon optional.
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:112:        # For now: drop the attributes (TODO).
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:113:        # Use at most 1 init-declarator.
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:114:        -> decl-specifier-seq init-declarator
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:115:        -> decl-specifier-seq declarator initializer
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:116:
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:117:        decl-specifier ->
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:118:              storage-class-specifier ->
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:119:                 (  "static" (only for member_object and function_object)
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:120:                  | "extern" (only for member_object and function_object)
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:121:                  | "register"
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:122:                 )
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:123:                 thread_local[opt] (only for member_object)
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:124:                                   (it can also appear before the others)
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:125:
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:126:            | type-specifier -> trailing-type-specifier
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:127:            | function-specifier -> "inline" | "virtual" | "explicit" (only
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:128:              for function_object)
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:129:            | "friend" (only for function_object)
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:130:            | "constexpr" (only for member_object and function_object)
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:131:        trailing-type-specifier ->
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:132:              simple-type-specifier
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:133:            | elaborated-type-specifier
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:134:            | typename-specifier
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:135:            | cv-qualifier -> "const" | "volatile"
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:136:        stricter grammar for decl-specifier-seq (with everything, each object
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:137:        uses a subset):
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:138:            visibility storage-class-specifier function-specifier "friend"
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:139:            "constexpr" "volatile" "const" trailing-type-specifier
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:140:            # where trailing-type-specifier can no be cv-qualifier
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:141:        # Inside e.g., template parameters a strict subset is used
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:142:        # (see type-specifier-seq)
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:143:        trailing-type-specifier ->
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:144:              simple-type-specifier ->
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:145:                ::[opt] nested-name-specifier[opt] type-name
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:146:              | ::[opt] nested-name-specifier "template" simple-template-id
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:147:              | "char" | "bool" | ect.
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:148:              | decltype-specifier
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:149:            | elaborated-type-specifier ->
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:150:                class-key attribute-specifier-seq[opt] ::[opt]
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:151:                nested-name-specifier[opt] identifier
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:152:              | class-key ::[opt] nested-name-specifier[opt] template[opt]
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:153:                simple-template-id
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:154:              | "enum" ::[opt] nested-name-specifier[opt] identifier
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:155:            | typename-specifier ->
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:156:                "typename" ::[opt] nested-name-specifier identifier
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:157:              | "typename" ::[opt] nested-name-specifier template[opt]
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:158:                simple-template-id
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:159:        class-key -> "class" | "struct" | "union"
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:160:        type-name ->* identifier | simple-template-id
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:161:        # ignoring attributes and decltype, and then some left-factoring
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:162:        trailing-type-specifier ->
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:163:            rest-of-trailing
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:164:            ("class" | "struct" | "union" | "typename") rest-of-trailing
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:165:            build-in -> "char" | "bool" | ect.
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:166:            decltype-specifier
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:167:        rest-of-trailing -> (with some simplification)
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:168:            "::"[opt] list-of-elements-separated-by-::
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:169:        element ->
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:170:            "template"[opt] identifier ("<" template-argument-list ">")[opt]
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:171:        template-argument-list ->
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:172:              template-argument "..."[opt]
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:173:            | template-argument-list "," template-argument "..."[opt]
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:174:        template-argument ->
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:175:              constant-expression
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:176:            | type-specifier-seq abstract-declarator
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:177:            | id-expression
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:178:
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:179:
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:180:        declarator ->
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:181:              ptr-declarator
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:182:            | noptr-declarator parameters-and-qualifiers trailing-return-type
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:183:        ptr-declarator ->
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:184:              noptr-declarator
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:185:            | ptr-operator ptr-declarator
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:186:        noptr-declarator ->
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:187:              declarator-id attribute-specifier-seq[opt] ->
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:188:                    "..."[opt] id-expression
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:189:                  | rest-of-trailing
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:190:            | noptr-declarator parameters-and-qualifiers
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:191:            | noptr-declarator "[" constant-expression[opt] "]"
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:192:              attribute-specifier-seq[opt]
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:193:            | "(" ptr-declarator ")"
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:194:        ptr-operator ->
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:195:              "*"  attribute-specifier-seq[opt] cv-qualifier-seq[opt]
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:196:            | "&   attribute-specifier-seq[opt]
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:197:            | "&&" attribute-specifier-seq[opt]
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:198:            | "::"[opt] nested-name-specifier "*" attribute-specifier-seq[opt]
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:199:                cv-qualifier-seq[opt]
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:200:        # function_object must use a parameters-and-qualifiers, the others may
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:201:        # use it (e.g., function poitners)
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:202:        parameters-and-qualifiers ->
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:203:            "(" parameter-clause ")" attribute-specifier-seq[opt]
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:204:            cv-qualifier-seq[opt] ref-qualifier[opt]
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:205:            exception-specification[opt]
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:206:        ref-qualifier -> "&" | "&&"
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:207:        exception-specification ->
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:208:            "noexcept" ("(" constant-expression ")")[opt]
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:209:            "throw" ("(" type-id-list ")")[opt]
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:210:        # TODO: we don't implement attributes
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:211:        # member functions can have initializers, but we fold them into here
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:212:        memberFunctionInit -> "=" "0"
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:213:        # (note: only "0" is allowed as the value, according to the standard,
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:214:        # right?)
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:215:
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:216:        enum-head ->
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:217:            enum-key attribute-specifier-seq[opt] nested-name-specifier[opt]
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:218:                identifier enum-base[opt]
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:219:        enum-key -> "enum" | "enum struct" | "enum class"
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:220:        enum-base ->
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:221:            ":" type
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:222:        enumerator-definition ->
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:223:              identifier
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:224:            | identifier "=" constant-expression
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:225:
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:226:    We additionally add the possibility for specifying the visibility as the
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:227:    first thing.
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:228:
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:229:    concept_object:
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:230:        goal:
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:231:            just a declaration of the name (for now)
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:232:
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:233:        grammar: only a single template parameter list, and the nested name
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:234:            may not have any template argument lists
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:235:
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:236:            "template" "<" template-parameter-list ">"
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:237:            nested-name-specifier
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:238:
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:239:    type_object:
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:240:        goal:
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:241:            either a single type (e.g., "MyClass:Something_T" or a typedef-like
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:242:            thing (e.g. "Something Something_T" or "int I_arr[]"
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:243:        grammar, single type: based on a type in a function parameter, but
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:244:        without a name:
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:245:               parameter-declaration
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:246:            -> attribute-specifier-seq[opt] decl-specifier-seq
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:247:               abstract-declarator[opt]
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:248:            # Drop the attributes
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:249:            -> decl-specifier-seq abstract-declarator[opt]
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:250:        grammar, typedef-like: no initilizer
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:251:            decl-specifier-seq declarator
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:252:        Can start with a templateDeclPrefix.
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:253:
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:254:    member_object:
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:255:        goal: as a type_object which must have a declarator, and optionally
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:256:        with a initializer
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:257:        grammar:
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:258:            decl-specifier-seq declarator initializer
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:259:        Can start with a templateDeclPrefix.
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:260:
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:261:    function_object:
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:262:        goal: a function declaration, TODO: what about templates? for now: skip
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:263:        grammar: no initializer
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:264:           decl-specifier-seq declarator
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:265:        Can start with a templateDeclPrefix.
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:266:
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:267:    class_object:
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:268:        goal: a class declaration, but with specification of a base class
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:269:        grammar:
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:270:              nested-name "final"[opt] (":" base-specifier-list)[opt]
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:271:            base-specifier-list ->
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:272:              base-specifier "..."[opt]
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:273:            | base-specifier-list, base-specifier "..."[opt]
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:274:            base-specifier ->
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:275:              base-type-specifier
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:276:            | "virtual" access-spe"cifier[opt]    base-type-specifier
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:277:            | access-specifier[opt] "virtual"[opt] base-type-specifier
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:278:        Can start with a templateDeclPrefix.
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:279:
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:280:    enum_object:
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:281:        goal: an unscoped enum or a scoped enum, optionally with the underlying
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:282:              type specified
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:283:        grammar:
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:284:            ("class" | "struct")[opt] visibility[opt] nested-name (":" type)[opt]
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:285:    enumerator_object:
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:286:        goal: an element in a scoped or unscoped enum. The name should be
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:287:              injected according to the scopedness.
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:288:        grammar:
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:289:            nested-name ("=" constant-expression)
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:290:
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:291:    namespace_object:
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:292:        goal: a directive to put all following declarations in a specific scope
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:293:        grammar:
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:294:            nested-name
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:295:"""
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:296:
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:297:udl_identifier_re = re.compile(r'''(?x)
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:298:    [a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*\b   # note, no word boundary in the beginning
sphinx/domains/cpp.py:299:''')

sphinx/domains/javascript.py:147:        """Handle object nesting before content

sphinx/domains/javascript.py:150:        constructs that are nestable, this method will build up a stack of the
sphinx/domains/javascript.py:151:        nesting hierarchy so that it can be later de-nested correctly, in

sphinx/domains/javascript.py:153:

sphinx/domains/javascript.py:155:        only the most recent object is tracked. This object prefix name will be
sphinx/domains/javascript.py:156:        removed with :py:meth:`after_content`.

sphinx/domains/javascript.py:162:                add the object prefix to this list. When we exit that object's
sphinx/domains/javascript.py:163:                nesting level, :py:meth:`after_content` is triggered and the
sphinx/domains/javascript.py:164:                prefix is removed from the end of the list.
sphinx/domains/javascript.py:165:
sphinx/domains/javascript.py:166:            js:object
sphinx/domains/javascript.py:167:                Current object prefix. This should generally reflect the last
sphinx/domains/javascript.py:168:                element in the prefix history

sphinx/domains/javascript.py:171:        if self.names:

sphinx/domains/javascript.py:173:            prefix = obj_name_prefix.strip('.') if obj_name_prefix else None
sphinx/domains/javascript.py:174:            if self.allow_nesting:

sphinx/domains/javascript.py:176:        if prefix:

sphinx/domains/javascript.py:178:            if self.allow_nesting:

sphinx/ext/extlinks.py:1:"""
sphinx/ext/extlinks.py:2:    sphinx.ext.extlinks
sphinx/ext/extlinks.py:3:    ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
sphinx/ext/extlinks.py:4:
sphinx/ext/extlinks.py:5:    Extension to save typing and prevent hard-coding of base URLs in the reST
sphinx/ext/extlinks.py:6:    files.
sphinx/ext/extlinks.py:7:
sphinx/ext/extlinks.py:8:    This adds a new config value called ``extlinks`` that is created like this::
sphinx/ext/extlinks.py:9:
sphinx/ext/extlinks.py:10:       extlinks = {'exmpl': ('https://example.invalid/%s.html', caption), ...}
sphinx/ext/extlinks.py:11:
sphinx/ext/extlinks.py:12:    Now you can use e.g. :exmpl:`foo` in your documents.  This will create a
sphinx/ext/extlinks.py:13:    link to ``https://example.invalid/foo.html``.  The link caption depends on
sphinx/ext/extlinks.py:14:    the *caption* value given:
sphinx/ext/extlinks.py:15:
sphinx/ext/extlinks.py:16:    - If it is ``None``, the caption will be the full URL.
sphinx/ext/extlinks.py:17:    - If it is a string, it must contain ``%s`` exactly once.  In this case the
sphinx/ext/extlinks.py:18:      caption will be *caption* with the role content substituted for ``%s``.
sphinx/ext/extlinks.py:19:
sphinx/ext/extlinks.py:20:    You can also give an explicit caption, e.g. :exmpl:`Foo <foo>`.
sphinx/ext/extlinks.py:21:
sphinx/ext/extlinks.py:22:    Both, the url string and the caption string must escape ``%`` as ``%%``.
sphinx/ext/extlinks.py:23:
sphinx/ext/extlinks.py:24:    :copyright: Copyright 2007-2021 by the Sphinx team, see AUTHORS.

sphinx/ext/extlinks.py:60:                          'contain exactly one \'%s\' and all other \'%\' need '

sphinx/ext/ifconfig.py:15:    namespace of the project configuration (that is, all variables from

sphinx/ext/intersphinx.py:8:

sphinx/ext/intersphinx.py:82:def _strip_basic_auth(url: str) -> str:
sphinx/ext/intersphinx.py:83:    """Returns *url* with basic auth credentials removed. Also returns the
sphinx/ext/intersphinx.py:84:    basic auth username and password if they're present in *url*.
sphinx/ext/intersphinx.py:85:
sphinx/ext/intersphinx.py:86:    E.g.: https://user:pass@example.com => https://example.com
sphinx/ext/intersphinx.py:87:
sphinx/ext/intersphinx.py:88:    *url* need not include basic auth credentials.
sphinx/ext/intersphinx.py:89:
sphinx/ext/intersphinx.py:90:    :param url: url which may or may not contain basic auth credentials
sphinx/ext/intersphinx.py:91:    :type url: ``str``
sphinx/ext/intersphinx.py:92:
sphinx/ext/intersphinx.py:93:    :return: *url* with any basic auth creds removed
sphinx/ext/intersphinx.py:94:    :rtype: ``str``
sphinx/ext/intersphinx.py:95:    """
sphinx/ext/intersphinx.py:96:    frags = list(urlsplit(url))
sphinx/ext/intersphinx.py:97:    # swap out "user[:pass]@hostname" for "hostname"
sphinx/ext/intersphinx.py:98:    if '@' in frags[1]:
sphinx/ext/intersphinx.py:99:        frags[1] = frags[1].split('@')[1]
sphinx/ext/intersphinx.py:100:    return urlunsplit(frags)

sphinx/ext/intersphinx.py:103:def _read_from_url(url: str, config: Config = None) -> IO:
sphinx/ext/intersphinx.py:104:    """Reads data from *url* with an HTTP *GET*.
sphinx/ext/intersphinx.py:105:
sphinx/ext/intersphinx.py:106:    This function supports fetching from resources which use basic HTTP auth as
sphinx/ext/intersphinx.py:107:    laid out by RFC1738 § 3.1. See § 5 for grammar definitions for URLs.
sphinx/ext/intersphinx.py:108:
sphinx/ext/intersphinx.py:109:    .. seealso:
sphinx/ext/intersphinx.py:110:
sphinx/ext/intersphinx.py:111:       https://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc1738.txt
sphinx/ext/intersphinx.py:112:
sphinx/ext/intersphinx.py:113:    :param url: URL of an HTTP resource
sphinx/ext/intersphinx.py:114:    :type url: ``str``
sphinx/ext/intersphinx.py:115:
sphinx/ext/intersphinx.py:116:    :return: data read from resource described by *url*
sphinx/ext/intersphinx.py:117:    :rtype: ``file``-like object
sphinx/ext/intersphinx.py:118:    """
sphinx/ext/intersphinx.py:119:    r = requests.get(url, stream=True, config=config, timeout=config.intersphinx_timeout)
sphinx/ext/intersphinx.py:120:    r.raise_for_status()
sphinx/ext/intersphinx.py:121:    r.raw.url = r.url
sphinx/ext/intersphinx.py:122:    # decode content-body based on the header.
sphinx/ext/intersphinx.py:123:    # ref: https://github.com/kennethreitz/requests/issues/2155
sphinx/ext/intersphinx.py:124:    r.raw.read = functools.partial(r.raw.read, decode_content=True)
sphinx/ext/intersphinx.py:125:    return r.raw

sphinx/jinja2glue.py:77:                    break

sphinx/roles.py:46:    A generic cross-referencing role.  To create a callable that can be used as

sphinx/roles.py:48:
sphinx/roles.py:49:    The general features of this role are:
sphinx/roles.py:50:

sphinx/roles.py:53:    * The implementation is a class rather than a function to make
sphinx/roles.py:54:      customization easier.

sphinx/roles.py:57:

sphinx/roles.py:63:        the reference and the content node

sphinx/transforms/post_transforms/images.py:156:    An image converter is kind of Docutils transform module.  It is used to
sphinx/transforms/post_transforms/images.py:157:    convert image files which does not supported by builder to appropriate

sphinx/transforms/post_transforms/images.py:162:    For such case, to use image converters allows to embed these
sphinx/transforms/post_transforms/images.py:163:    unsupported images into the document.  One of image converters;
sphinx/transforms/post_transforms/images.py:164:    :ref:`sphinx.ext.imgconverter <sphinx.ext.imgconverter>` can convert
sphinx/transforms/post_transforms/images.py:165:    a SVG image to PNG format using Imagemagick internally.
sphinx/transforms/post_transforms/images.py:166:
sphinx/transforms/post_transforms/images.py:167:    There are three steps to make your custom image converter:
sphinx/transforms/post_transforms/images.py:168:
sphinx/transforms/post_transforms/images.py:169:    1. Make a subclass of ``ImageConverter`` class
sphinx/transforms/post_transforms/images.py:170:    2. Override ``conversion_rules``, ``is_available()`` and ``convert()``

sphinx/util/inspect.py:410:    """A getattr() that turns all exceptions into AttributeErrors."""
sphinx/util/inspect.py:411:    try:

sphinx/util/inspect.py:415:        # NotImplementedError), so let's try to read the attribute directly
sphinx/util/inspect.py:416:        try:
sphinx/util/inspect.py:417:            # In case the object does weird things with attribute access
sphinx/util/inspect.py:418:            # such that accessing `obj.__dict__` may raise an exception
sphinx/util/inspect.py:419:            return obj.__dict__[name]
sphinx/util/inspect.py:420:        except Exception:
sphinx/util/inspect.py:421:            pass
sphinx/util/inspect.py:422:

sphinx/util/inspect.py:424:        # with attribute access
sphinx/util/inspect.py:425:        if defargs:
sphinx/util/inspect.py:426:            return defargs[0]
sphinx/util/inspect.py:427:
sphinx/util/inspect.py:428:        raise AttributeError(name) from exc

sphinx/util/matching.py:17:def _translate_pattern(pat: str) -> str:
sphinx/util/matching.py:18:    """Translate a shell-style glob pattern to a regular expression.
sphinx/util/matching.py:19:
sphinx/util/matching.py:20:    Adapted from the fnmatch module, but enhanced so that single stars don't
sphinx/util/matching.py:21:    match slashes.
sphinx/util/matching.py:22:    """
sphinx/util/matching.py:23:    i, n = 0, len(pat)
sphinx/util/matching.py:24:    res = ''
sphinx/util/matching.py:25:    while i < n:
sphinx/util/matching.py:26:        c = pat[i]
sphinx/util/matching.py:27:        i += 1
sphinx/util/matching.py:28:        if c == '*':
sphinx/util/matching.py:29:            if i < n and pat[i] == '*':
sphinx/util/matching.py:30:                # double star matches slashes too
sphinx/util/matching.py:31:                i += 1
sphinx/util/matching.py:32:                res = res + '.*'
sphinx/util/matching.py:33:            else:
sphinx/util/matching.py:34:                # single star doesn't match slashes
sphinx/util/matching.py:35:                res = res + '[^/]*'
sphinx/util/matching.py:36:        elif c == '?':
sphinx/util/matching.py:37:            # question mark doesn't match slashes too
sphinx/util/matching.py:38:            res = res + '[^/]'
sphinx/util/matching.py:39:        elif c == '[':
sphinx/util/matching.py:40:            j = i
sphinx/util/matching.py:41:            if j < n and pat[j] == '!':
sphinx/util/matching.py:42:                j += 1
sphinx/util/matching.py:43:            if j < n and pat[j] == ']':
sphinx/util/matching.py:44:                j += 1
sphinx/util/matching.py:45:            while j < n and pat[j] != ']':
sphinx/util/matching.py:46:                j += 1
sphinx/util/matching.py:47:            if j >= n:
sphinx/util/matching.py:48:                res = res + '\\['
sphinx/util/matching.py:49:            else:
sphinx/util/matching.py:50:                stuff = pat[i:j].replace('\\', '\\\\')
sphinx/util/matching.py:51:                i = j + 1
sphinx/util/matching.py:52:                if stuff[0] == '!':
sphinx/util/matching.py:53:                    # negative pattern mustn't match slashes too
sphinx/util/matching.py:54:                    stuff = '^/' + stuff[1:]
sphinx/util/matching.py:55:                elif stuff[0] == '^':
sphinx/util/matching.py:56:                    stuff = '\\' + stuff
sphinx/util/matching.py:57:                res = '%s[%s]' % (res, stuff)
sphinx/util/matching.py:58:        else:
sphinx/util/matching.py:59:            res += re.escape(c)
sphinx/util/matching.py:60:    return res + '$'

sphinx/util/matching.py:64:    return [re.compile(_translate_pattern(pat)).match for pat in patterns]

sphinx/util/osutil.py:174:class FileAvoidWrite:
sphinx/util/osutil.py:175:    """File-like object that buffers output and only writes if content changed.
sphinx/util/osutil.py:176:
sphinx/util/osutil.py:177:    Use this class like when writing to a file to avoid touching the original
sphinx/util/osutil.py:178:    file if the content hasn't changed. This is useful in scenarios where file
sphinx/util/osutil.py:179:    mtime is used to invalidate caches or trigger new behavior.
sphinx/util/osutil.py:180:
sphinx/util/osutil.py:181:    When writing to this file handle, all writes are buffered until the object
sphinx/util/osutil.py:182:    is closed.
sphinx/util/osutil.py:183:
sphinx/util/osutil.py:184:    Objects can be used as context managers.
sphinx/util/osutil.py:185:    """
sphinx/util/osutil.py:186:    def __init__(self, path: str) -> None:
sphinx/util/osutil.py:187:        self._path = path
sphinx/util/osutil.py:188:        self._io: Optional[StringIO] = None
sphinx/util/osutil.py:189:
sphinx/util/osutil.py:190:    def write(self, data: str) -> None:
sphinx/util/osutil.py:191:        if not self._io:
sphinx/util/osutil.py:192:            self._io = StringIO()
sphinx/util/osutil.py:193:        self._io.write(data)
sphinx/util/osutil.py:194:
sphinx/util/osutil.py:195:    def close(self) -> None:
sphinx/util/osutil.py:196:        """Stop accepting writes and write file, if needed."""
sphinx/util/osutil.py:197:        if not self._io:
sphinx/util/osutil.py:198:            raise Exception('FileAvoidWrite does not support empty files.')
sphinx/util/osutil.py:199:
sphinx/util/osutil.py:200:        buf = self.getvalue()
sphinx/util/osutil.py:201:        self._io.close()
sphinx/util/osutil.py:202:
sphinx/util/osutil.py:203:        try:
sphinx/util/osutil.py:204:            with open(self._path, encoding='utf-8') as old_f:
sphinx/util/osutil.py:205:                old_content = old_f.read()
sphinx/util/osutil.py:206:                if old_content == buf:
sphinx/util/osutil.py:207:                    return
sphinx/util/osutil.py:208:        except OSError:
sphinx/util/osutil.py:209:            pass
sphinx/util/osutil.py:210:
sphinx/util/osutil.py:211:        with open(self._path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
sphinx/util/osutil.py:212:            f.write(buf)

sphinx/util/parallel.py:144:def make_chunks(arguments: Sequence[str], nproc: int, maxbatch: int = 10) -> List[Any]:
sphinx/util/parallel.py:145:    # determine how many documents to read in one go
sphinx/util/parallel.py:146:    nargs = len(arguments)
sphinx/util/parallel.py:147:    chunksize = nargs // nproc
sphinx/util/parallel.py:148:    if chunksize >= maxbatch:
sphinx/util/parallel.py:149:        # try to improve batch size vs. number of batches
sphinx/util/parallel.py:150:        chunksize = int(sqrt(nargs / nproc * maxbatch))
sphinx/util/parallel.py:151:    if chunksize == 0:
sphinx/util/parallel.py:152:        chunksize = 1
sphinx/util/parallel.py:153:    nchunks, rest = divmod(nargs, chunksize)
sphinx/util/parallel.py:154:    if rest:
sphinx/util/parallel.py:155:        nchunks += 1
sphinx/util/parallel.py:156:    # partition documents in "chunks" that will be written by one Process
sphinx/util/parallel.py:157:    return [arguments[i * chunksize:(i + 1) * chunksize] for i in range(nchunks)]

sphinx/util/stemmer/porter.py:18:    The algorithm as described in the paper could be exactly replicated
sphinx/util/stemmer/porter.py:19:    by adjusting the points of DEPARTURE, but this is barely necessary,
sphinx/util/stemmer/porter.py:20:    because (a) the points of DEPARTURE are definitely improvements, and
sphinx/util/stemmer/porter.py:21:    (b) no encoding of the Porter stemmer I have seen is anything like
sphinx/util/stemmer/porter.py:22:    as exact as this version, even with the points of DEPARTURE!

sphinx/util/stemmer/porter.py:50:        """cons(i) is TRUE <=> b[i] is a consonant."""
sphinx/util/stemmer/porter.py:51:        if self.b[i] == 'a' or self.b[i] == 'e' or self.b[i] == 'i' \
sphinx/util/stemmer/porter.py:52:           or self.b[i] == 'o' or self.b[i] == 'u':

sphinx/util/stemmer/porter.py:57:            else:
sphinx/util/stemmer/porter.py:58:                return (not self.cons(i - 1))

sphinx/versioning.py:50:def merge_doctrees(old: Node, new: Node, condition: Any) -> Iterator[Node]:
sphinx/versioning.py:51:    """Merge the `old` doctree with the `new` one while looking at nodes
sphinx/versioning.py:52:    matching the `condition`.
sphinx/versioning.py:53:
sphinx/versioning.py:54:    Each node which replaces another one or has been added to the `new` doctree
sphinx/versioning.py:55:    will be yielded.
sphinx/versioning.py:56:
sphinx/versioning.py:57:    :param condition:
sphinx/versioning.py:58:        A callable which returns either ``True`` or ``False`` for a given node.
sphinx/versioning.py:59:    """
sphinx/versioning.py:60:    old_iter = old.traverse(condition)
sphinx/versioning.py:61:    new_iter = new.traverse(condition)
sphinx/versioning.py:62:    old_nodes = []
sphinx/versioning.py:63:    new_nodes = []
sphinx/versioning.py:64:    ratios = {}
sphinx/versioning.py:65:    seen = set()
sphinx/versioning.py:66:    # compare the nodes each doctree in order
sphinx/versioning.py:67:    for old_node, new_node in zip_longest(old_iter, new_iter):
sphinx/versioning.py:68:        if old_node is None:
sphinx/versioning.py:69:            new_nodes.append(new_node)
sphinx/versioning.py:70:            continue
sphinx/versioning.py:71:        if not getattr(old_node, 'uid', None):
sphinx/versioning.py:72:            # maybe config.gettext_uuid has been changed.
sphinx/versioning.py:73:            old_node.uid = uuid4().hex
sphinx/versioning.py:74:        if new_node is None:
sphinx/versioning.py:75:            old_nodes.append(old_node)
sphinx/versioning.py:76:            continue
sphinx/versioning.py:77:        ratio = get_ratio(old_node.rawsource, new_node.rawsource)
sphinx/versioning.py:78:        if ratio == 0:
sphinx/versioning.py:79:            new_node.uid = old_node.uid
sphinx/versioning.py:80:            seen.add(new_node)
sphinx/versioning.py:81:        else:
sphinx/versioning.py:82:            ratios[old_node, new_node] = ratio
sphinx/versioning.py:83:            old_nodes.append(old_node)
sphinx/versioning.py:84:            new_nodes.append(new_node)
sphinx/versioning.py:85:    # calculate the ratios for each unequal pair of nodes, should we stumble
sphinx/versioning.py:86:    # on a pair which is equal we set the uid and add it to the seen ones
sphinx/versioning.py:87:    for old_node, new_node in product(old_nodes, new_nodes):
sphinx/versioning.py:88:        if new_node in seen or (old_node, new_node) in ratios:
sphinx/versioning.py:89:            continue
sphinx/versioning.py:90:        ratio = get_ratio(old_node.rawsource, new_node.rawsource)
sphinx/versioning.py:91:        if ratio == 0:
sphinx/versioning.py:92:            new_node.uid = old_node.uid
sphinx/versioning.py:93:            seen.add(new_node)
sphinx/versioning.py:94:        else:
sphinx/versioning.py:95:            ratios[old_node, new_node] = ratio
sphinx/versioning.py:96:    # choose the old node with the best ratio for each new node and set the uid
sphinx/versioning.py:97:    # as long as the ratio is under a certain value, in which case we consider
sphinx/versioning.py:98:    # them not changed but different
sphinx/versioning.py:99:    ratios = sorted(ratios.items(), key=itemgetter(1))  # type: ignore
sphinx/versioning.py:100:    for (old_node, new_node), ratio in ratios:
sphinx/versioning.py:101:        if new_node in seen:
sphinx/versioning.py:102:            continue
sphinx/versioning.py:103:        else:
sphinx/versioning.py:104:            seen.add(new_node)
sphinx/versioning.py:105:        if ratio < VERSIONING_RATIO:
sphinx/versioning.py:106:            new_node.uid = old_node.uid
sphinx/versioning.py:107:        else:
sphinx/versioning.py:108:            new_node.uid = uuid4().hex
sphinx/versioning.py:109:            yield new_node
sphinx/versioning.py:110:    # create new uuids for any new node we left out earlier, this happens
sphinx/versioning.py:111:    # if one or more nodes are simply added.
sphinx/versioning.py:112:    for new_node in set(new_nodes) - seen:
sphinx/versioning.py:113:        new_node.uid = uuid4().hex
sphinx/versioning.py:114:        yield new_node
sphinx/versioning.py:115:
sphinx/versioning.py:116:
sphinx/versioning.py:117:def get_ratio(old: str, new: str) -> float:
sphinx/versioning.py:118:    """Return a "similarity ratio" (in percent) representing the similarity
sphinx/versioning.py:119:    between the two strings where 0 is equal and anything above less than equal.
sphinx/versioning.py:120:    """
sphinx/versioning.py:121:    if not all([old, new]):
sphinx/versioning.py:122:        return VERSIONING_RATIO
sphinx/versioning.py:123:
sphinx/versioning.py:124:    if IS_SPEEDUP:
sphinx/versioning.py:125:        return Levenshtein.distance(old, new) / (len(old) / 100.0)
sphinx/versioning.py:126:    else:
sphinx/versioning.py:127:        return levenshtein_distance(old, new) / (len(old) / 100.0)
sphinx/versioning.py:128:
sphinx/versioning.py:129:
sphinx/versioning.py:130:def levenshtein_distance(a: str, b: str) -> int:
sphinx/versioning.py:131:    """Return the Levenshtein edit distance between two strings *a* and *b*."""
sphinx/versioning.py:132:    if a == b:
sphinx/versioning.py:133:        return 0
sphinx/versioning.py:134:    if len(a) < len(b):
sphinx/versioning.py:135:        a, b = b, a
sphinx/versioning.py:136:    if not a:
sphinx/versioning.py:137:        return len(b)
sphinx/versioning.py:138:    previous_row = list(range(len(b) + 1))
sphinx/versioning.py:139:    for i, column1 in enumerate(a):
sphinx/versioning.py:140:        current_row = [i + 1]
sphinx/versioning.py:141:        for j, column2 in enumerate(b):
sphinx/versioning.py:142:            insertions = previous_row[j + 1] + 1
sphinx/versioning.py:143:            deletions = current_row[j] + 1
sphinx/versioning.py:144:            substitutions = previous_row[j] + (column1 != column2)
sphinx/versioning.py:145:            current_row.append(min(insertions, deletions, substitutions))
sphinx/versioning.py:146:        previous_row = current_row
sphinx/versioning.py:147:    return previous_row[-1]

sphinx/writers/latex.py:134:    def get_table_type(self) -> str:
sphinx/writers/latex.py:135:        """Returns the LaTeX environment name for the table.
sphinx/writers/latex.py:136:
sphinx/writers/latex.py:137:        The class currently supports:
sphinx/writers/latex.py:138:
sphinx/writers/latex.py:139:        * longtable
sphinx/writers/latex.py:140:        * tabular
sphinx/writers/latex.py:141:        * tabulary
sphinx/writers/latex.py:142:        """
sphinx/writers/latex.py:143:        if self.is_longtable():
sphinx/writers/latex.py:144:            return 'longtable'
sphinx/writers/latex.py:145:        elif self.has_verbatim:
sphinx/writers/latex.py:146:            return 'tabular'
sphinx/writers/latex.py:147:        elif self.colspec:
sphinx/writers/latex.py:148:            return 'tabulary'
sphinx/writers/latex.py:149:        elif self.has_problematic or (self.colwidths and 'colwidths-given' in self.classes):
sphinx/writers/latex.py:150:            return 'tabular'
sphinx/writers/latex.py:151:        else:
sphinx/writers/latex.py:152:            return 'tabulary'
sphinx/writers/latex.py:153:
sphinx/writers/latex.py:154:    def get_colspec(self) -> str:
sphinx/writers/latex.py:155:        """Returns a column spec of table.
sphinx/writers/latex.py:156:
sphinx/writers/latex.py:157:        This is what LaTeX calls the 'preamble argument' of the used table environment.
sphinx/writers/latex.py:158:
sphinx/writers/latex.py:159:        .. note:: the ``\\X`` and ``T`` column type specifiers are defined in ``sphinx.sty``.
sphinx/writers/latex.py:160:        """
sphinx/writers/latex.py:161:        if self.colspec:
sphinx/writers/latex.py:162:            return self.colspec
sphinx/writers/latex.py:163:        elif self.colwidths and 'colwidths-given' in self.classes:
sphinx/writers/latex.py:164:            total = sum(self.colwidths)
sphinx/writers/latex.py:165:            colspecs = [r'\X{%d}{%d}' % (width, total) for width in self.colwidths]
sphinx/writers/latex.py:166:            return '{|%s|}' % '|'.join(colspecs) + CR
sphinx/writers/latex.py:167:        elif self.has_problematic:
sphinx/writers/latex.py:168:            return r'{|*{%d}{\X{1}{%d}|}}' % (self.colcount, self.colcount) + CR
sphinx/writers/latex.py:169:        elif self.get_table_type() == 'tabulary':
sphinx/writers/latex.py:170:            # sphinx.sty sets T to be J by default.
sphinx/writers/latex.py:171:            return '{|' + ('T|' * self.colcount) + '}' + CR
sphinx/writers/latex.py:172:        elif self.has_oldproblematic:
sphinx/writers/latex.py:173:            return r'{|*{%d}{\X{1}{%d}|}}' % (self.colcount, self.colcount) + CR
sphinx/writers/latex.py:174:        else:
sphinx/writers/latex.py:175:            return '{|' + ('l|' * self.colcount) + '}' + CR

sphinx/writers/latex.py:244:def rstdim_to_latexdim(width_str: str, scale: int = 100) -> str:
sphinx/writers/latex.py:245:    """Convert `width_str` with rst length to LaTeX length."""
sphinx/writers/latex.py:246:    match = re.match(r'^(\d*\.?\d*)\s*(\S*)$', width_str)
sphinx/writers/latex.py:247:    if not match:
sphinx/writers/latex.py:248:        raise ValueError
sphinx/writers/latex.py:249:    res = width_str
sphinx/writers/latex.py:250:    amount, unit = match.groups()[:2]
sphinx/writers/latex.py:251:    if scale == 100:
sphinx/writers/latex.py:252:        float(amount)  # validate amount is float
sphinx/writers/latex.py:253:        if unit in ('', "px"):
sphinx/writers/latex.py:254:            res = r"%s\sphinxpxdimen" % amount
sphinx/writers/latex.py:255:        elif unit == 'pt':
sphinx/writers/latex.py:256:            res = '%sbp' % amount  # convert to 'bp'
sphinx/writers/latex.py:257:        elif unit == "%":
sphinx/writers/latex.py:258:            res = r"%.3f\linewidth" % (float(amount) / 100.0)
sphinx/writers/latex.py:259:    else:
sphinx/writers/latex.py:260:        amount_float = float(amount) * scale / 100.0
sphinx/writers/latex.py:261:        if unit in ('', "px"):
sphinx/writers/latex.py:262:            res = r"%.5f\sphinxpxdimen" % amount_float
sphinx/writers/latex.py:263:        elif unit == 'pt':
sphinx/writers/latex.py:264:            res = '%.5fbp' % amount_float
sphinx/writers/latex.py:265:        elif unit == "%":
sphinx/writers/latex.py:266:            res = r"%.5f\linewidth" % (amount_float / 100.0)
sphinx/writers/latex.py:267:        else:
sphinx/writers/latex.py:268:            res = "%.5f%s" % (amount_float, unit)
sphinx/writers/latex.py:269:    return res

sphinx/writers/latex.py:2010:    def encode_uri(self, text: str) -> str:

sphinx/writers/manpage.py:43:class NestedInlineTransform:
sphinx/writers/manpage.py:44:    """
sphinx/writers/manpage.py:45:    Flatten nested inline nodes:
sphinx/writers/manpage.py:46:
sphinx/writers/manpage.py:47:    Before:
sphinx/writers/manpage.py:48:        <strong>foo=<emphasis>1</emphasis>
sphinx/writers/manpage.py:49:        &bar=<emphasis>2</emphasis></strong>
sphinx/writers/manpage.py:50:    After:
sphinx/writers/manpage.py:51:        <strong>foo=</strong><emphasis>var</emphasis>
sphinx/writers/manpage.py:52:        <strong>&bar=</strong><emphasis>2</emphasis>
sphinx/writers/manpage.py:53:    """
sphinx/writers/manpage.py:54:    def __init__(self, document: nodes.document) -> None:
sphinx/writers/manpage.py:55:        self.document = document
sphinx/writers/manpage.py:56:
sphinx/writers/manpage.py:57:    def apply(self, **kwargs: Any) -> None:
sphinx/writers/manpage.py:58:        matcher = NodeMatcher(nodes.literal, nodes.emphasis, nodes.strong)
sphinx/writers/manpage.py:59:        for node in self.document.traverse(matcher):  # type: TextElement
sphinx/writers/manpage.py:60:            if any(matcher(subnode) for subnode in node):
sphinx/writers/manpage.py:61:                pos = node.parent.index(node)
sphinx/writers/manpage.py:62:                for subnode in reversed(node[1:]):
sphinx/writers/manpage.py:63:                    node.remove(subnode)
sphinx/writers/manpage.py:64:                    if matcher(subnode):
sphinx/writers/manpage.py:65:                        node.parent.insert(pos + 1, subnode)
sphinx/writers/manpage.py:66:                    else:
sphinx/writers/manpage.py:67:                        newnode = node.__class__('', '', subnode, **node.attributes)
sphinx/writers/manpage.py:68:                        node.parent.insert(pos + 1, newnode)

sphinx/writers/texinfo.py:346:    # -- Escaping
sphinx/writers/texinfo.py:347:    # Which characters to escape depends on the context.  In some cases,

sphinx/writers/texinfo.py:349:    # characters.
sphinx/writers/texinfo.py:350:
sphinx/writers/texinfo.py:351:    def escape(self, s: str) -> str:
sphinx/writers/texinfo.py:352:        """Return a string with Texinfo command characters escaped."""
sphinx/writers/texinfo.py:353:        s = s.replace('@', '@@')
sphinx/writers/texinfo.py:354:        s = s.replace('{', '@{')
sphinx/writers/texinfo.py:355:        s = s.replace('}', '@}')
sphinx/writers/texinfo.py:356:        # prevent `` and '' quote conversion
sphinx/writers/texinfo.py:357:        s = s.replace('``', "`@w{`}")
sphinx/writers/texinfo.py:358:        s = s.replace("''", "'@w{'}")
sphinx/writers/texinfo.py:359:        return s
sphinx/writers/texinfo.py:360:
sphinx/writers/texinfo.py:361:    def escape_arg(self, s: str) -> str:
sphinx/writers/texinfo.py:362:        """Return an escaped string suitable for use as an argument
sphinx/writers/texinfo.py:363:        to a Texinfo command."""
sphinx/writers/texinfo.py:364:        s = self.escape(s)
sphinx/writers/texinfo.py:365:        # commas are the argument delimiters
sphinx/writers/texinfo.py:366:        s = s.replace(',', '@comma{}')
sphinx/writers/texinfo.py:367:        # normalize white space
sphinx/writers/texinfo.py:368:        s = ' '.join(s.split()).strip()
sphinx/writers/texinfo.py:369:        return s
sphinx/writers/texinfo.py:370:
sphinx/writers/texinfo.py:371:    def escape_id(self, s: str) -> str:
sphinx/writers/texinfo.py:372:        """Return an escaped string suitable for node names and anchors."""
sphinx/writers/texinfo.py:373:        bad_chars = ',:()'
sphinx/writers/texinfo.py:374:        for bc in bad_chars:
sphinx/writers/texinfo.py:375:            s = s.replace(bc, ' ')
sphinx/writers/texinfo.py:376:        if re.search('[^ .]', s):
sphinx/writers/texinfo.py:377:            # remove DOTs if name contains other characters
sphinx/writers/texinfo.py:378:            s = s.replace('.', ' ')
sphinx/writers/texinfo.py:379:        s = ' '.join(s.split()).strip()
sphinx/writers/texinfo.py:380:        return self.escape(s)

sphinx/writers/texinfo.py:457:        if not unit or unit == "px":

tests/test_writer_latex.py:17:    # Length units docutils supported

tests/test_writer_latex.py:28:
